mainTopic: זבין and מצורעין during a פסח brought in טומאה; where and when שתי הלחם and לחם הפנים are prepared, and whether the oven or the שולחן makes them holy
overview: The amud opens by finishing a ברייתא of רבי אליעזר. From a פסוק that lists צרוע, זב and טמא לנפש together, he learns that זבין and מצורעין follow טמאי מתים. So when the פסח is brought in טומאה, they are not liable for entering. Then a new משנה teaches that the dough for שתי הלחם and לחם הפנים is kneaded and shaped outside the עזרה, baked inside, and does not override שבת. רבי יהודה says everything is done inside, and רבי שמעון says the breads are כשר even in בית פאגי. The גמרא finds the תנא קמא's words hard. Its question first concerns which vessel makes the flour holy. It then sharpens into a different problem: if the oven makes the bread holy, bread baked before שבת should become פסול through לינה. An answer given in רב אשי's name, that 'inside' means a place of careful כהנים, is rejected as a mistake. רבי אבהו בר כהנא then shows that רבי יהודה and רבי שמעון read the same פסוק about דוד at נוב in opposite ways: is the bread made holy by the oven or by the שולחן? Finally, the גמרא points out that דוד received bread already removed from the שולחן, and it rereads his words as an argument that he may eat the לחם הפנים.

steps.title: רבי אליעזר raises a possibility about זבין and מצורעין
steps.stepSummary: רבי אליעזר asks: if זבין and מצורעין pushed into the עזרה during a פסח brought in טומאה, would they be חייב?
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אליעזר says: You might think that if זבין and מצורעין pushed their way into the עזרה during a פסח that is brought in טומאה, they would be liable.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אליעזר sets up a question: what if זבין and מצורעין force their way into the עזרה on a day when the פסח is brought in טומאה? He is preparing the ground for a פסוק that will answer it in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When most of the nation is טמא מת, the פסח is brought anyway, and טמאי מתים may enter. But זבין and מצורעין have a more severe טומאה. So you might assume they would still be fully liable for entering. The word יכול shows this is only a possible assumption that the next step will reject.

keyTerms.meaning: People with a bodily discharge that makes them טמא
People with צרעת (biblical skin affliction)
The Temple courtyard
A פסח offering brought even in impurity, because most of the people are טמא מת
"One might think": introduces an assumption that will be rejected
Liable to punishment (here, כרת)

phrases.english: Rabbi Eliezer says:
One might think: if zavim and lepers pushed their way
and entered the Temple courtyard
during a Pesach offering brought in impurity
one might think they would be liable?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the earlier discussion about who is sent out of which camp; brings רבי אליעזר's ברייתא.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Sets up the assumption that זבין and מצורעין entering during a פסח brought in טומאה might be liable.

steps.title: The פסוק links זבין and מצורעין to טמאי מתים
steps.stepSummary: From the פסוק that lists צרוע, זב and טמא לנפש together, רבי אליעזר learns that they go together. When טמאי מתים are sent out, so are זבין and מצורעין, and when they are not, neither are the others.
steps.simpleTranslation: The פסוק teaches: "That they send out from the camp any צרוע and any זב and anyone טמא לנפש." When טמאי מתים are sent out, זבין and מצורעין are sent out. When טמאי מתים are not sent out, זבין and מצורעין are not sent out.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אליעזר answers his own question with a פסוק. The three types of טומאה are listed together, so they share the same rule about being sent out.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rejected idea was that זבין and מצורעין are always liable, because their טומאה is more severe. The פסוק puts all three in one list, so their liability is tied together. On a day when טמאי מתים are allowed in, זבין and מצורעין are not liable for entering either.

keyTerms.meaning: "The verse teaches": introduces a פסוק as the source
Camp; here, the holy area that a טמא person must leave
People made טמא by contact with a dead body
Are sent out

steps.whatToRemember: According to רבי אליעזר, זבין and מצורעין follow טמאי מתים. If טמאי מתים are not sent out (as in a פסח brought in טומאה), זבין and מצורעין are not liable for entering.
steps.confusionAlert: Saying "they are not sent out" here means they are not liable for entering. It does not mean זבין and מצורעין are invited in.

phrases.english: The verse teaches:
"That they send out from the camp
any leper and any zav
and anyone impure from a corpse"
At a time when those impure from the dead are sent out,
zavim and lepers are sent out.
When those impure from the dead are not sent out,
zavim and lepers are not sent out.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the assumption raised in step 1 with a פסוק.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: They are not liable, because the פסוק ties זבין and מצורעין to טמאי מתים. When טמאי מתים are not sent out, neither are they.

steps.title: משנה: kneading outside, baking inside, no overriding שבת
steps.stepSummary: The new משנה teaches that for שתי הלחם and לחם הפנים, kneading and shaping are done outside the עזרה and baking inside, and their preparation does not override שבת.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: Both שתי הלחם and לחם הפנים are kneaded and shaped outside the עזרה, but baked inside, and their preparation does not override שבת.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. The תנא קמא gives the rule for where two special breads are made, and says making them does not push aside שבת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה divides the process into two stages. The early stages (kneading and shaping) are done outside the עזרה, and the baking is done inside. It also rules that preparing these breads cannot be done on שבת. The two rulings will soon be compared to each other.

keyTerms.meaning: The two loaves offered on שבועות
The shewbread placed weekly on the שולחן in the Temple
Kneading the dough and shaping the loaves
Baking
Override שבת (may be done on שבת)

phrases.english: Mishnah:
Both the two loaves
and the shewbread:
their kneading and their shaping are outside
phrases.notes: "Outside" here means outside the Temple courtyard.

phrases.english: and their baking is inside,
and they do not override Shabbat.

steps.triggerLanguage: אַחַת שְׁתֵּי הַלֶּחֶם, וְאַחַת לֶחֶם הַפָּנִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה on a new topic.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Kneading and shaping are done outside the עזרה, baking inside, and preparation does not override שבת.

steps.title: רבי יהודה: everything is done inside
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה disagrees and says that every step of making these breads is done inside the עזרה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהודה says: All of their procedures are done inside.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יהודה gives a second opinion in the משנה: kneading, shaping and baking are all done inside the עזרה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The תנא קמא put only the baking inside. רבי יהודה moves the whole process inside, so even the kneading and shaping happen in the עזרה.

keyTerms.meaning: All of their procedures (kneading, shaping, baking)
Inside the Temple courtyard

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda says:
All of their procedures are inside.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר: כׇּל מַעֲשֵׂיהֶם בִּפְנִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Disagrees with the תנא קמא in step 3.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: All stages of making שתי הלחם and לחם הפנים take place inside the עזרה.

steps.title: רבי שמעון: כשר in the עזרה and in בית פאגי
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמעון says one should always say that שתי הלחם and לחם הפנים are כשר whether made in the עזרה or in בית פאגי.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי שמעון says: Always be used to saying that שתי הלחם and לחם הפנים are כשר in the עזרה and כשר in בית פאגי.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי שמעון gives a third, more lenient opinion. These breads are כשר even if prepared in בית פאגי, outside the עזרה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The תנא קמא and רבי יהודה both require at least the baking to be inside. רבי שמעון says the breads are כשר even if made in בית פאגי, outside the Temple Mount. His opinion goes the furthest away from רבי יהודה's.

keyTerms.meaning: Always be accustomed to say: a firm, general statement
Valid, fit for use
A place outside the Temple Mount

steps.whatToRemember: The משנה has three opinions. The תנא קמא says kneading and shaping are outside and baking is inside. רבי יהודה says everything is inside. רבי שמעון says the breads are כשר even in בית פאגי.

phrases.english: Rabbi Shimon says:
Always be accustomed to say
that the two loaves and the shewbread
are fit in the courtyard
and fit in Beit Pagei.
phrases.notes: בית פאגי is a place outside the Temple Mount.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A third opinion, more lenient than both earlier ones.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: שתי הלחם and לחם הפנים are כשר whether prepared in the עזרה or in בית פאגי.

steps.title: The משנה's first opinion seems to contradict itself
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא opens by saying the תנא קמא's statement is difficult in itself.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא announces that the תנא קמא's words in the משנה seem to clash with each other. This is a setup line, and the גמרא will explain the problem in the next lines.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words "הא גופא קשיא" mean the problem comes from inside the same statement, not from another source. The challenge is aimed at the תנא קמא's rulings in step 3. The details are not spelled out yet.

keyTerms.meaning: "This itself is difficult": a statement seems to contradict itself
A difficulty or challenge

phrases.english: Gemara:
This itself is difficult:
phrases.notes: The גמרא means the first opinion in the משנה clashes with itself. The explanation comes right after this.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins the גמרא's analysis of the תנא קמא's ruling in the משנה.
steps.kashyaTarget: The תנא קמא's statement in the משנה (step 3)
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The parts of the תנא קמא's own statement seem to contradict each other. The specific contradiction is explained in the following lines.

steps.title: Kneading outside but baking inside seems to contradict itself
steps.stepSummary: The תנא קמא's two rules seem to give opposite answers about whether the dry measuring vessel makes flour holy. רבה praises רב ששת as the one who raised this.
steps.simpleTranslation: You said kneading and shaping happen outside, so the dry measure must not make the flour holy. You also said baking happens inside, so the dry measure must make it holy! רבה said: a man as tough as iron asked this, and that is רב ששת.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now spells out the difficulty it announced in the last step: the two halves of the תנא קמא's rule seem to clash.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the measuring vessel made the flour holy, it could not be kneaded outside the עזרה. If it did not make the flour holy, there would be no reason to bake it inside. So each half of the משנה points to a different answer.

keyTerms.meaning: The holy vessel used to measure dry things like flour
Apparently / this shows that
Became holy (was made a vessel that makes things holy)

phrases.english: You said: their kneading and their shaping are done outside —
apparently the dry measure was not made holy,
and their baking is done inside —
apparently the dry measure was made holy!
רבה said: a tough man raised this difficulty,
who is as tough as iron,
and who is he? רב ששת.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Spells out the internal contradiction announced in step 6
steps.kashyaTarget: The תנא קמא's rule that kneading is done outside and baking inside
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The kneading rule implies the measure does not make the flour holy, while the baking rule implies it does.

steps.title: Maybe the oven, not the measure, makes the bread holy
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the question. The עשרון might not make the flour holy while the oven does, so there is no contradiction.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the difficulty? Maybe the עשרון does not make it holy, but the oven does.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on רב ששת's question and shows a simple way the משנה can make sense.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question assumed the only thing that could make the bread holy is the measuring vessel. If the oven is what makes it holy, the flour can be kneaded outside. It still has to be baked inside, because the oven is the vessel that makes it holy.

keyTerms.meaning: A tenth of an איפה, the measure used for this flour
Oven
Makes holy

phrases.english: What is the difficulty?
Perhaps the tenth-measure does not make it holy,
but the oven makes it holy.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי קַשְׁיָא? דִּלְמָא עִשָּׂרוֹן לָא מְקַדֵּשׁ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the contradiction raised in step 7
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The whole contradiction about the dry measure
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: It wrongly assumes the measuring vessel is the only thing that could make the bread holy; the oven could be what does it.

steps.title: If the oven makes it holy, the bread would become פסול overnight
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא changes the question. If the oven makes the bread holy, and baking does not override שבת, the bread would be baked before שבת and become פסול by staying overnight. Now רבא praises רב ששת for this question.
steps.simpleTranslation: If there is a difficulty, this is it: baking is done inside, so the oven makes it holy. But the baking does not override שבת, so it would become פסול from staying overnight! רבא said: a man as tough as iron asked this, and that is רב ששת.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא accepts that the oven makes the bread holy, and then shows a new problem that comes from that.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since the baking cannot be done on שבת, it must be done earlier. Once the oven makes the bread holy, leaving it overnight before it is placed should make it פסול through לינה. So the משנה still seems hard to explain. The praise is now said by רבא and is attached to this better question.

keyTerms.meaning: If there is a difficulty, this is the real one
They do not override שבת
Staying overnight, which makes holy items פסול

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up רבה (step 7) with רבא (here). The גמרא moves the praise of רב ששת from רבה's version of the question to רבא's sharper version.

phrases.english: Rather, if there is a difficulty, this is the difficulty:
and their baking is done inside,
apparently the oven makes it holy,
and yet they do not override שבת —
it would become פסול by staying overnight!

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא אָמַר רָבָא: הִקְשָׁה אָדָם קָשֶׁה,
phrases.english: Rather, רבא said: a tough man raised this difficulty,
who is as tough as iron,
and who is he? רב ששת.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on step 8's idea that the oven makes the bread holy, and finds a new problem with it
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's two rules: baking is done inside, and preparation does not override שבת
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the oven makes the bread holy, baking it before שבת means it stays overnight while holy and becomes פסול through לינה.

steps.title: 'Inside' means a place with careful כהנים
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי answers that 'inside' may not mean inside the עזרה. It may mean a place with careful people, so the oven need not make the bread holy at all.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי said: What is the difficulty? Maybe 'inside' means in a place where the people are careful.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי answers רב ששת's question by reading the word 'inside' in a new way.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question depended on 'inside' meaning the baking must be in the עזרה, which made it seem the oven makes the bread holy. If 'inside' only means a place with careful כהנים, the oven does not make the bread holy. Then baking before שבת causes no problem of לינה.

keyTerms.meaning: Careful, alert people (here the כהנים)
Inside

steps.whatToRemember: The question went from 'which vessel makes it holy?' to 'why doesn't the bread become פסול overnight?'. רב אשי tries to answer that 'inside' means a place of careful כהנים, not inside the עזרה. The next step rejects this answer as a mistake.

phrases.english: רב אשי said: What is the difficulty?
Perhaps what does 'inside' mean —
in a place of careful people.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב אָשֵׁי: מַאי קוּשְׁיָא? דִּלְמָא מַאי מִבִּפְנִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the לינה question of step 9
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reading the word 'inside' in a new way
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'Inside' means inside the עזרה, which shows the oven makes the bread holy, so it should become פסול overnight
steps.terutzMaskana: 'Inside' means a place of careful כהנים, so the oven does not make the bread holy and there is no problem of לינה

steps.title: The answer given in רב אשי's name is a mistake
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects רב אשי's answer. If careful people are needed for baking, they should also be needed for kneading and shaping. If not, they should not be needed for baking either. So the statement given in his name must be an error.
steps.simpleTranslation: This statement of רב אשי is a mistake. Look at it either way. If baking needs careful people, kneading and shaping should need them too. If kneading and shaping do not need careful people, baking should not need them either. So the statement of רב אשי is a mistake.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects the answer from step 10 and says it was wrongly said in רב אשי's name.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה says kneading and shaping are done 'outside' and baking 'inside'. רב אשי said 'inside' just means a place with careful people. But nothing makes baking need more care than kneading and shaping, so his reading cannot explain why the משנה splits them. That means the question of step 9 comes back.

keyTerms.meaning: A mistaken statement, one that was wrongly said in someone's name
'Whichever way you look at it'. Both possible ways lead to a problem

steps.whyThisMatters: Once רב אשי's answer is rejected, the problem from step 9 stands again: if the תנור makes the bread holy, baking before שבת should make it פסול through לינה. The גמרא gives no new answer here.

phrases.english: And this statement of רב אשי is a mistake,
phrases.notes: He means the answer from step 10. The גמרא says it was never really his.

phrases.english: whichever way you look at it:
if for baking we need careful people,
then for kneading and shaping we also [need] careful people;
phrases.notes: The word in square brackets is part of the corrected wording.

phrases.english: and if for kneading [and shaping] we do not need careful people,
then for baking we also do not need careful people.
Rather, the statement of רב אשי is a mistake.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָא דְּרַב אָשֵׁי בְּרוּתָא הִיא, מָה נַפְשָׁךְ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the answer of step 10, so the question of step 9 stands again.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The whole answer of רב אשי, that 'inside' means a place of careful people
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: It cannot explain why the משנה treats baking differently from kneading and shaping, since all of them would need the same level of care.

steps.title: Both sages learn from the same פסוק
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes רבי יהודה from the משנה, that everything is done inside. רבי אבהו בר כהנא says that רבי יהודה and רבי שמעון both learn their views from one פסוק: דוד's words 'והוא דרך חל אף כי היום יקדש בכלי'.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: רבי יהודה says all their work is done inside, etc. רבי אבהו בר כהנא said: Both of them learned from the same פסוק: 'And it is a weekday way, even though today it will be made holy in the vessel.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to a new part of the משנה, the argument between רבי יהודה and רבי שמעון. It is setting up the next two steps, which show how each sage reads the פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהודה says even the baking must be done inside the עזרה. רבי אבהו בר כהנא says the two sages do not argue from different sources. They share one פסוק and read it in two different ways.

keyTerms.meaning: Inside, meaning inside the עזרה (the Temple courtyard)
One פסוק
They explained a פסוק to learn a law from it
A weekday or ordinary way
It will become holy in the vessel

phrases.english: רבי יהודה says:
All their work is done inside, [etc.]
רבי אבהו בר כהנא said:
And both of them learned from the same פסוק:
'And it is a weekday way,'
phrases.notes: שמואל א 21:6. These are דוד's words when he asks for bread at נוב.

phrases.english: 'even though today it will be made holy in the vessel.'

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי אֲבָהוּ בַּר כָּהֲנָא: וּשְׁנֵיהֶן מִקְרָא אֶחָד דָּרְשׁוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the רב אשי discussion and starts on the next part of the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי יהודה and רבי שמעון both base their views on the same פסוק in שמואל א.

steps.title: How רבי יהודה reads the פסוק
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה says דוד found the כהנים baking the לחם הפנים on a weekday. He told them it should be baked on שבת, because the oven makes it holy right away, so bread baked earlier becomes פסול by staying overnight.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהודה holds: דוד found them baking it on a weekday. He said to them: Are you baking it in a weekday way? 'Even though today it will become holy in the vessel.' It will become פסול by staying overnight.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains רבי יהודה's reading. דוד was criticizing the כהנים for baking the bread on a weekday.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבי יהודה, 'the vessel' is the תנור. Once baked, the bread is already holy, so if it is baked before שבת it stays overnight and becomes פסול. That is why it must be baked on שבת itself, inside the עזרה.

keyTerms.meaning: A weekday, not שבת
Staying overnight. Holy food left past its time becomes פסול
It becomes disqualified (פסול)

phrases.english: רבי יהודה holds:
he found them baking it on a weekday.
phrases.notes: 'He' is דוד, and 'them' are the כהנים baking the לחם הפנים.

phrases.english: He said to them:
Are you baking it in a weekday way?
'Even though today it will become holy in the vessel'!
phrases.notes: For רבי יהודה, 'the vessel' is the oven.

phrases.english: It will become disqualified by staying overnight.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה סָבַר: בַּחוֹל אַשְׁכְּחִינְהוּ דְּקָא אָפוּ לֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Fills in the first of the two readings that step 12 promised.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The תנור makes the לחם הפנים holy, so it must be baked on שבת in the עזרה to avoid becoming פסול by staying overnight.

steps.title: How רבי שמעון reads the פסוק
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמעון says דוד found the כהנים baking the לחם הפנים on שבת. He told them it should be baked on a weekday, because the oven does not make it holy. Only the שולחן does.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי שמעון holds: דוד found them baking it on שבת. He said to them: Don't you need to do it in a weekday way? Does the oven make it holy? It is the שולחן that makes it holy.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains רבי שמעון's reading. דוד was criticizing the כהנים for baking the bread on שבת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבי שמעון, the bread is not holy until it is put on the שולחן. So baking it before שבת causes no problem of staying overnight, and there is no reason to bake on שבת. This also explains why the baking can be done outside the עזרה.

keyTerms.meaning: Oven
The Table in the מקדש where the לחם הפנים is placed
Makes something holy

steps.whatToRemember: The core argument: רבי יהודה holds the תנור makes the לחם הפנים holy (so it is baked on שבת, inside). רבי שמעון holds only the שולחן makes it holy (so it is baked on a weekday and may be baked outside).
steps.confusionAlert: The same words 'דרך חול' are a criticism in both readings, but in opposite directions. For רבי יהודה, דוד complains they baked on a weekday. For רבי שמעון, דוד complains they did not bake on a weekday.

phrases.english: רבי שמעון holds:
he found them baking it on שבת.
He said to them:
Don't you need to do it in a weekday way?!
Does the oven make it holy?!
It is the שולחן that makes it holy.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן סָבַר: בְּשַׁבָּת אַשְׁכְּחִינְהוּ דְּקָא אָפוּ לֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the second reading of the same פסוק, the opposite of רבי יהודה's in step 13.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The תנור does not make the לחם הפנים holy; only the שולחן does, so it should be baked on a weekday.

steps.title: The verse shows דוד did not find them at baking time
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the idea, shared by both רבי יהודה and רבי שמעון, that דוד found the כהנים while they were baking. The פסוק says the bread he got was taken from before ה׳, meaning it had already been on the שולחן.
steps.simpleTranslation: How can you say דוד found them at the time of baking? The פסוק says: 'And the כהן gave him holy bread, for there was no bread there except the לחם הפנים that was taken from before ה׳.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the background story that both רבי יהודה and רבי שמעון assumed. It quotes a פסוק showing that the bread דוד received had already been removed from the שולחן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both opinions pictured דוד walking in while the כהנים were baking and teaching them the right day to bake. But the פסוק describes bread 'taken from before ה׳', which is old bread removed from the שולחן, not fresh bread in the oven. So the setting does not fit the פסוק.

keyTerms.meaning: Baking
He found them
The showbread, the twelve loaves placed on the שולחן each שבת
That were removed (taken away)
But it is written! (a challenge from a פסוק)

steps.confusionAlert: This question is not against one side only. It challenges the story both רבי יהודה and רבי שמעון used, since both said דוד found them baking.

phrases.english: And can you really say
that he found them at the time of baking?
But it is written: 'And the priest gave him holy bread,
for there was no bread there
except the showbread
that was taken from before the Lord'!
phrases.notes: שמואל א כא:ז. 'Taken from before ה׳' means it had already been on the שולחן and was now removed.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמִי מָצֵית אָמְרַתְּ דְּבִשְׁעַת אֲפִיָּיה אַשְׁכְּחִינְהוּ? וְהָכְתִיב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the shared background story behind both readings in Steps 13-14.
steps.kashyaTarget: The assumption, shared by רבי יהודה and רבי שמעון, that דוד found the כהנים while they were baking.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The פסוק says the bread דוד received was already 'removed from before ה׳'. That means old bread taken off the שולחן, not bread being baked, so the scene was not baking time.

steps.title: So what did דוד mean by 'דרך חל'?
steps.stepSummary: Since the baking story does not work, the גמרא asks what דוד's words 'דרך חל' actually meant when he said them to the כהנים.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, what is the meaning of 'it is a חול way', which דוד said to them?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא accepts the challenge and asks for a new meaning of דוד's words. This step sets up the next step, where the new reading is given.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With the baking story gone, the phrase 'והוא דרך חל אף כי היום יקדש בכלי' needs a new setting. The גמרא is asking what conversation these words belong to.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather, what is it? (asking for a new explanation after the old one failed)
A non-holy (everyday) way or matter

phrases.english: Rather, what is 'a non-holy way',
which he said to them?

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא מַאי ״דֶּרֶךְ חֹל״, דְּקָא אָמַר לְהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Follows from the challenge in Step 15 and asks for a new reading of the פסוק.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The real meaning and setting of דוד's words 'דרך חל, אף כי היום יקדש בכלי'.

steps.title: דוד asks to eat the לחם הפנים
steps.stepSummary: The כהנים told דוד that the only bread available was the holy לחם הפנים. דוד answered that the bread already removed is like חול, so of course he may eat it. And even today's bread, placed in the כלי today, could be given to him to eat.
steps.simpleTranslation: The כהנים told him: There is no bread here except the לחם הפנים that was removed from before ה׳. He told them: This bread is obvious. Once it is out of the rules of מעילה, it is like חול. But even the other bread, the one that 'today becomes holy in the כלי', give it to him so he can eat.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the new reading: דוד's words were his reply when the כהנים said they only had holy bread. He argued that he was allowed to eat it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'דרך חל' now means that the removed bread is no longer under מעילה, so it counts as חול in that sense. 'אף כי היום יקדש בכלי' now means 'even the bread made holy today', which could also be given to him. The phrase is no longer about which day to bake, so the baking-time problem from Step 15 is gone.

keyTerms.meaning: The law against using holy property for yourself
It is not even necessary to say (this case is obvious)
That other one
Becomes holy in the vessel
Give him so he can eat

steps.whatToRemember: The גמרא rejects reading 'דרך חל' as a teaching about baking day, since the פסוק shows דוד received removed bread. Instead it reads the words as דוד's argument that he may eat the לחם הפנים: the removed bread for sure, and even today's bread.
steps.confusionAlert: 'דרך חל' here does not mean the bread is simply ordinary bread anyone may eat. It means the bread is out of מעילה, so it is no longer treated like holy property in that way.
steps.whyThisMatters: This new reading fits the פסוק quoted in Step 15, which shows דוד received bread already taken off the שולחן. דוד's words become his argument that he may eat the bread, rather than a scene at baking time.

phrases.english: This is what they said to him:
phrases.notes: 'They' are the כהנים, and 'him' is דוד.

phrases.english: There is no bread,
except 'the showbread
that was taken from before the Lord'.
He said to them: Not only this one,
for since it has left the rules of misusing holy property,
it is in a non-holy state,
but even that other one too,
which 'today becomes holy in the vessel',
give it to him so he may eat,
phrases.notes: דוד is speaking about himself here, so 'give him' really means 'give me'.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָכִי קָא אָמְרוּ לֵיהּ: לֵיכָּא לֶחֶם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 16 with a new reading that fits the פסוק cited in Step 15.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: דוד's words were his reply to the כהנים, who said only לחם הפנים was available. He said the removed bread is out of מעילה and counts as חול, and even today's newly holy bread could be given to him to eat.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reinterpretation of the פסוק's setting and meaning
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'דרך חל' and 'היום יקדש בכלי' were a teaching to the כהנים about which day to bake.
steps.terutzMaskana: The words were part of דוד's request to eat the bread: the removed bread is out of מעילה, and even today's bread could be given to him.
